text:
monitoring-bot: [ALERT] eu-west-1 GPU pool 'hosted-gpu-a' saturation >95% for 3m. Admission control enabled for lowest-priority tenants.

sarah: seeing a ton of queueing on hosted-serving-{*} for small token workloads, latency jumps to 800-1200ms.

akshay: confirmed, our admission metrics show dropped requests and backlog length spikes around 14:12 UTC. Dashboards look odd — headroom graph flat at 0 for last 10m.

mohit: fwiw, I just checked our metrics pipeline, prometheus-forwarder had a restart at 14:05. Could be ingestion lag making dashboards stale.

sarah: so real saturation or just stale numbers? app teams are seeing 429 from admission-control.

amon: @mohit do we have raw telemetry to tell if kernels actually peaked?

mohit: raw node-level GPU util and container queues show sustained 98% GPU util on a subset of nodes for last 6m. Not just dashboard lag. The forwarder restart made the aggregated headroom panel read 0 earlier than reality.

jamie: possible short-term blast from a client doing many short completions. Do we know which model or tenant?

akshay: tenant-id: t-frontend-42 has a correlated spike in request rate (x6). Model: opt-13b-8k-hosted.

sarah: that tenant is low-priority but not blacklisted; admission-control should shed them first but it's also hitting some medium-prio routes.

jamie: immediate mitigation options: 1) push stricter admission weight for t-frontend-42, 2) lower max_batch_size on that route, 3) temporarily increase min_replicas for hosted-gpu-a (costly). Thoughts?

mohit: prefer #1 + #2. Quick change to admission rules is sub-second. Scaling min_replicas will take minutes and costs extra.

sarah: can someone run the admission tweak and patch a route config?

akshay: doing admission tweak now: ```curl -X POST https://infra-api.internal/configs/admission -d '{"tenant":"t-frontend-42","weight":0.2}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx'``` applying..

akshay: applied. Monitor shows dropped rate for that tenant up to 60% now. Queue length trending down.

mohit: also pushed a temporary route override to reduce max_batch_size for opt-13b-8k-hosted: ```rbctl patch route hosted-opt-13b --max-batch 8 --env eu-west-1``` — will let it stabilize.

sarah: visible improvement: tail latency back to ~220ms, admission 429s for that tenant only. Good.

jamie: next steps: 1) investigate why that tenant spiked (billing/abuse), 2) ensure dashboards reflect node-level metrics even if forwarder restarts, 3) consider autoscale policy change for short-burst traffic.

mohit: on dashboards: I'll add a fallback to show per-node metrics directly from node-exporter when aggregated stream is stale. Also will add alert if forwarder has restart in last 5m.

akshay: cost note — if we keep min_replicas higher in euw1 to handle these bursts it will add ~3-4k USD/month. Flagging for finance if we change default.

sarah: can we schedule a canary policy for short-burst autoscaling that prioritizes low-latency over price for 30s windows?

jamie: yes — design doc needed. I'll open a ticket and assign owners. For now, keep the admission tweak active for 15m then relax unless spike persists.

mohit: adding postmortem checklist item: attribute spike to t-frontend-42 API change? We'll ask platform-sdks team to correlate deploys.

sarah: thanks all. I'll message the oncall rotations and impacted app owners. Closing thread once metrics stable for 20m. :thumbsup:

monitoring-bot: RESOLVED eu-west-1 GPU pool 'hosted-gpu-a' saturation back under 70% — automated admission rollback scheduled in 15m if stable.

jamie: leaving the admission-tweak as a short-lived mitigation. Will follow up with doc and a small runbook for similar incidents.

sarah: pairing with @mohit to write the dashboard fallback PR later today.

end.
